plain_english: Now the use of this path, our present subject, is set forth.
sanskrit_cite: athādhvano@sya prakṛta upayogaḥ prakāśyate

plain_english: Thus this whole path, as it rests in consciousness, through that rests also in void, intellect, breath, channel-wheels, and bodies.
sanskrit_cite: itthamadhvā samasto@yaṃ yathā saṃvidi saṃsthitaḥ | taddvārā śūnyadhīprāṇanāḍīcakratanuṣvatho

plain_english: And outside too, everywhere in liṅga, image, fire, altar and the rest; so it stands, whole and part-wise, in sequence and all at once.
sanskrit_cite: bahiśca liṅgamūrtyagnisthaṇḍilādiṣu sarvataḥ | tathā sthitaḥ samastaśca vyastaścaiṣa kramākramāt

plain_english: Laid out from consciousness-principle to the outer, this path: at each level one should make one's own form shine, by own freedom, in fitting form.
sanskrit_cite: āsaṃvittattvamābāhyaṃ yo@yamadhvā vyavasthitaḥ | tatra tatrocitaṃ rūpaṃ svaṃ svātantryeṇa bhāsayet

plain_english: And everything's form everywhere — even his does not not shine; for we cannot bear exclusion anywhere, even in dream.
sanskrit_cite: sarvaṃ sarvatra rūpaṃ ca tasyāpi na na bhāsate | nahyavaccheditāṃ kvāpi svapne@pi viṣahāmahe

plain_english: Thus one should behold the body as filled with the universe-path, painted by time's activity — the abode of pulsation made of space and time.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ viśvādhvasaṃpūrṇaṃ kālavyāpāracitritam | deśakālamayaspandasadma dehaṃ vilokayet

plain_english: So beheld, he is made of the deities within the universe; to be meditated, worshipped, libated — entered then, one is freed.
sanskrit_cite: tathā vilokyamāno@sau viśvāntardevatāmayaḥ | dhyeyaḥ pūjyaśca tarpyaśca tadāviṣṭo vimucyate

plain_english: Thus pot, cloth, liṅga, altar, book, water — or whatever one may see anywhere: there one should reach identity-with-that.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ ghaṭaṃ paṭaṃ liṅgaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ pustakaṃ jalam | yadvā kiṃcitkvacitpaśyettatra tanmayatāṃ vrajet

plain_english: Therein offering of things is held worship through non-difference; and contemplation of full-formedness is called meditation.
sanskrit_cite: tatrārpaṇaṃ hi vastūnāmabhedenārcanaṃ matam | tathā saṃpūrṇarūpatvānusaṃdhirdhyānamucyate

plain_english: Unshaking contemplation of fullness brings firmness; and through inner-mutter practice, reflecting, one becomes a mantra-vessel.
sanskrit_cite: saṃpūrṇatvānusaṃdhānamakampaṃ dārḍhyamānayan | tathāntarjalpayogena vimṛśañjapabhājanam

plain_english: Effecting the melting of self-difference of the beings offered therein, their ray-rich being he should bestow — devoted to the fire-rite.
sanskrit_cite: tatrārpitānāṃ bhāvānāṃ svakabhedavilāpanam | kurvaṃstadraśmisadbhāvaṃ dadyāddhomakriyāparaḥ

plain_english: For one so acting, seeing all with equal eye, unwaveringness is the pure vow — evenness taught in the Nandiśikhā.
sanskrit_cite: tathaivaṃkurvataḥ sarvaṃ samabhāvena paśyataḥ | niṣkampatā vrataṃ śuddhaṃ sāmyaṃ nandiśikhoditam

plain_english: Thus through worship, japa, meditation, fire-offering, vow, and rule in sequence, the ancients called the complete state absorption.
sanskrit_cite: tathārcanajapadhyānahomavratavidhikramāt | paripūrṇāṃ sthitiṃ prāhuḥ samādhiṃ guravaḥ purā

plain_english: Here in worship, japa and the rest, whether outward or inward, there is no rule at all about materials, nor any prohibition.
sanskrit_cite: atra pūjājapādyeṣu bahirantardvayasthitau | dravyaughe na vidhiḥ ko@pi na kāpi pratiṣiddhatā

plain_english: No use here whatsoever for visualization, purification, twilight-rites and the rest; and in the Trika Sūtra it is said sacrifice arises toward the rite.
sanskrit_cite: kalpanāśuddhisaṃdhyādernopayogo@tra kaścana | uktaṃ śrītrikasūtre ca jāyate yajanaṃ prati

plain_english: Not knowing rule, knowing rule, and 'thus' and so on at length: when, as, by which, where one's own consciousness is gracious.
sanskrit_cite: avidhijño vidhijñaścetyevamādi suvistaram | yadā yathā yena yatra svā samvittiḥ prasīdati

plain_english: Then, so, by that, there: each respective enjoyable — and that is the rule; all, worldly and unworldly, one should employ here by that.
sanskrit_cite: tadā tathā tena tatra tattadbhogyaṃ vidhiśca saḥ | laukikālaukikaṃ sarvaṃ tenātra viniyojayet

plain_english: In steadiness: but the trembler should forcibly diminish tremor — by force, as, by whatever means, in sequence or all at once, or.
sanskrit_cite: niṣkampatve sakampastu kampaṃ nirhrāsayedbalāt | yathā yenābhyupāyena kramādakramato@pi vā

plain_english: Doubt melts within — so he should become striving; the goddesses resting in mind, rite, and senses he should libate with forbidden things indeed.
sanskrit_cite: vicikitsā galatyantastathāsau yatnavānbhavet | dhīkarmākṣagatā devīrniṣiddhaireva tarpayet

plain_english: And the hero-vow one should salute — thus the Bhargaśikhā word: for doubt is impurity, weariness, contraction — thus this.
sanskrit_cite: vīravrataṃ cābhinandediti bhargaśikhāvacaḥ | tathāhi śaṅkā mālinyaṃ glāniḥ saṃkoca ityadaḥ

plain_english: Inside the world-prison it forges gross-post shackles; mantras are letter-natured, substance five-elemented.
sanskrit_cite: saṃsārakārāgārāntaḥ sthūlasthūṇāghaṭāyate | mantrā varṇasvabhāvā ye dravyaṃ yatpāñcabhautikam

plain_english: The breathing kind which is consciousness-selfed — where is mixture there, how? With mixture absent, what is this doubt — even hers clearly baseless.
sanskrit_cite: yaccidātma prāṇijātaṃ tatra kaḥ saṃkaraḥ katham | saṃkarābhāvataḥ keyaṃ śaṅkā tasyāmapi sphuṭam

plain_english: One should not doubt; thus doubt dissolves through disregard — in the Sarvācāra, Vīrālī, Niśācara, Krama and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: na śaṅketa tathā śaṅkā vilīyetāvahelayā | śrīsarvācāravīrālīniśācarakramādiṣu

plain_english: And this is spread in the śāstras — there it is said: for from doubt arises weariness, from doubt being a vessel of obstacles.
sanskrit_cite: śāstreṣu vitataṃ caitattatra tatrocyate | yataḥ śaṅkayā jāyate glāniḥ śaṅkayā vighnabhājanam

plain_english: And said Utpaladeva, the venerable guru of my guru: the all-doubt thunderbolt path — we bow to the Māheśvara path.
sanskrit_cite: uvācotpaladevaśca śrīmānasmadgurorguruḥ | sarvāśaṅkāśaniṃ mārgaṃ numo māheśvaraṃ tviti

plain_english: For attaining the anuttara state, this āṇava with means shown at great length — indeed, make it grow, O wise ones!
sanskrit_cite: anuttarapadāptaye tadidamāṇavaṃ darśitābhyupāyamativistarānnanu | vidāṃkurudhvaṃ budhāḥ
